title: Local state vs server state vs URL state
description: Understand the differences between local state, server state, and URL state in React. Learn when each kind of state is appropriate, how to choose the right tool, and how to avoid common architecture mistakes.

data.text: Not all state in a React application is the same. Some values live only inside a single component, others live on a remote server, and a third kind is encoded directly into the URL. Treating these three kinds of state as interchangeable is one of the most common sources of bugs in medium-to-large React applications.

In this lesson, we build a clear mental model for **local state**, **server state**, and **URL state**. For each kind, you will learn its lifetime, who owns it, where it is stored, and which React features or libraries are the best fit.

Local state is state that belongs to a single component (or a small subtree) and disappears when the component unmounts. It is the default kind of state in React, created with `useState` or `useReducer`.

data.title: Typical examples of local state
items: Whether a dropdown menu is open
The current value of a text input that has not been submitted yet
A loading spinner that appears while an event handler runs
A tab selection inside a reusable widget

data.title: Local state example — a search filter panel
data.content: A filter panel keeps its selected categories in local state because those selections are UI-only and do not need to survive a page reload.

data.text: Server state is data that originates from a backend and is fetched over the network. It is inherently asynchronous, can become stale, and must be synchronized with the server. Despite being stored remotely, many apps incorrectly place server state into local React state or even into Context.

data.title: Do not treat server state as local state
data.text: Caching API responses inside `useState` leads to stale data, race conditions, and missing loading or error states. Use a purpose-built server-state library such as TanStack Query, SWR, or Apollo Client instead.

data.title: Server state with TanStack Query
data.content: The query library manages caching, background refetching, and loading/error states automatically.

data.text: URL state is any piece of state that is encoded in the browser's address bar. Because the URL is the single shared source of truth across tabs, it can be bookmarked, refreshed, and shared. It is the right home for filters, pagination, sort order, and selected IDs that define what the user is currently looking at.

data.title: Good candidates for URL state
items: Active filters on a search results page
The current page number in a paginated list
The selected tab inside a settings page
A product ID in a product detail view
Search query text entered by the user

data.title: URL state with React Router
data.content: The search query is synchronized with the URL query string using `useSearchParams`, so users can bookmark their filtered view.

rows: Until URL changes or bookmark is deleted

data.title: Decision checklist
items: Does the value describe what the user is currently viewing or filtering? Put it in URL state.
Does the value come from an API call and may change independently of the UI? Put it in server state.
Is the value UI-only, ephemeral, and scoped to one component tree? Put it in local state.

data.title: Architecture check
data.text: Before adding a new piece of state, ask: who owns it, where should the single source of truth live, and what should happen when the user refreshes the page? The answers usually point directly at one of the three kinds.

data.title: Exercise: classify some state
data.description: Given a dashboard page with a date-range picker, a list of notifications fetched from an API, and a sidebar collapse toggle, classify each piece of state as local, server, or URL state and explain your reasoning.
data.expectedOutcome: You should place the date range in URL state, the notifications in server state using a query library, and the sidebar toggle in local state.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Local state is ephemeral and component-scoped.
Server state should be managed by a dedicated server-state library.
URL state is bookmarkable, shareable, and the natural home for filters and navigation.
The right boundary between these three kinds prevents stale data, race conditions, and lost navigation context.
data.takeaway: Before reaching for useState or Context, ask which of the three state owners should actually hold the value.
